title: Canonical-composite reconstruction: each member's 8x8 feature map must repaint the per-pixel MEDIAN of the three training surveys (a picture of Berlin in which anything seen in only one survey is gone), through a training-only decoder that never flies
hypothesis: Nine experiments on this ruler leave the held-out 2024 photograph at 7.5% usable / 17% false fix (exp 7, 1.096) with usable never outside 7-12.5%, and they say, read together, that the deployed feature of a place is still built from survey-specific content: exp 5 lifted the TRAINING photographs to 72-81% usable at the same held-out viewpoints and 2024 did not move (12.5%), so the trunk learns three survey-specific layouts; exp 4's photometric randomisation (the only mechanism that ever moved 2024 accuracy, 7% -> 11.75%) removed the GLOBAL part of a survey change, and the remaining part is CONTENT - shadows of a different sun, parked cars, construction, canopy state, true-ortho artefacts - which no per-view photometric draw can synthesise. Three attempts to make the feature survey-invariant through the three surveys themselves did not get a fair test: exp 3's cosine term was vacuous on non-negative GAP features (0.966 at epoch 1), exp 9's batch-standardised within-place variance penalty at weight 10 destroyed training outright (train top1 0.008 after 8 epochs, member 0 collapsed to a constant answer, xsurvey_agree 0.74 at top1 0.0003 - a training collapse, NOT a verdict on invariance; it is recorded here so it is not read as one), and exp 8's external teacher gave the student a target it could not reach (student-teacher cosine 0.40 against the 0.55 needed; the teacher's own cross-survey cosine was only 0.46-0.53). The common failure is the TARGET: a latent-consistency target can be satisfied for free or collapse, and a 22M-parameter teacher's semantics are not representable by a 1M-parameter CNN. This experiment gives the trunk a target that is survey-invariant BY CONSTRUCTION, cannot collapse, cannot be satisfied for free, and is trivially representable: the per-pixel median of the three training captures after per-survey global colour normalisation. The captures are pixel-aligned on one grid (<= 1 px), so at every pixel the median keeps the value two or three surveys agree on and discards whatever is unique to one photograph: a car, that survey's shadow where the other two are lit, one season's canopy, one year's construction, the leaning roof of the standard DOP against the two true orthos. Design-stage probe on the three TRAINING captures only (runs/_probe_exp10_canon.py, 300 random lattice places at random headings, 4 m/px standardised crops; truedop_2024 never opened): two real surveys of the same place correlate 0.575-0.622 with each other, while each survey correlates 0.812-0.851 with the composite - the composite is the picture the three photographs have in common, and it is much closer to every one of them than they are to each other, so a view from ANY survey can be asked to produce it; nearest-neighbour retrieval over the 300 places from one survey to the composite is 96-100% when aligned (and 12-20% under the eval's 12 px shift - shift tolerance remains the CNN's job, exactly as exp 6's probe found for survey-to-survey matching). Mechanism: a training-only decoder per member (two 3x3 convs with 2x upsampling, ~84k parameters, discarded before export) takes that member's 8x8x112 trunk feature map of its augmented own-survey view and must repaint the composite crop of the same position and heading at 32x32 (4 m/px), standardised per crop per channel so exposure and colour balance are not part of the target; MSE against it is added to the member's loss at weight 3. Each of the 64 feature cells then has to carry the stable coarse structure of its own 16 px patch (inside its 31 px receptive field - exp 5's 'bag of 31 m texture patches' becomes a bag of canonical-structure patches) and is paid nothing for carrying the survey-specific content the median removed; the pooled vector the cell head reads is a sum of exactly those descriptors. This is the library's L1-B (training-only reconstruction auxiliary, 'lives entirely in the never-flies lane') and L2's rule (predict a target that does not move; every expensive part is scaffolding dropped before export), re-aimed from lighting canonicalisation to survey canonicalisation, and it is the four-area era's exps 23/24/43 (redraw-the-clean-daytime-crop auxiliaries, verdicts void, measured on never-seen ground under a median metric) given a target that only this era's data asset makes possible: there was one photograph per place then, and a median needs three. It differs from exp 6 (blends as INPUTS: ghosted, physically meaningless frames the model had to classify) in that the composite is a TARGET and the inputs stay real photographs; from exp 8 in that the target is an image a two-layer decoder can certainly paint from 112-d local features, not a foundation model's semantics; and from exps 3/9 in that a fixed pixel-space target has no vacuous optimum (chance MSE is 1.0 by construction) and no collapsed one (a constant prediction scores exactly chance). The deployed graph is unchanged byte-for-byte (3,942,411 bytes).
method: model/model.py: Member gains forward_train(x) -> (logits, offset, fmap) alongside the untouched forward(); a new training-only CanonDecoder (8x8x112 -> 32x32x3, not a submodule of CellLocNet, never exported) and constants CANON_PX = 32, RECON_WEIGHT = 3.0. model/train.py: after the training captures are resident on the device, build_canonical() computes once, from those captures only, the per-pixel per-channel median of the globally colour-normalised surveys as a uint8 [1,3,H,W] raster; per mini-batch the composite crop at the batch's own (cx, cy, heading) is cut with the existing gpu_crops(), average-pooled 4x to 32x32 and standardised per crop per channel; each member's own decoder repaints it from the fmap of that member's augmented view and MSE x 3.0 is added to the member's tent-CE + offset loss. Decoder parameters join the same Adam/cosine optimiser; per-member recon MSE is logged per epoch; export is unchanged.
expected_outcome: Mechanical checks that must hold or the mechanism did not bite: the logged per-member reconstruction MSE (chance = 1.0 by construction of the standardised target) falls below 0.5 for both members by epoch 8, with the loss falling monotonically; per-member augmented top1 ends within 0.05 of exp 7's 0.35 and the member agreement rate at or above 0.33 (the auxiliary must not have crowded out the cell task - exp 9's collapse signature, top1 near 0.001, would mean the weight is wrong, not that the idea is); exported bytes read exactly 3,942,411 and host latency ~2 ms (the deployed graph is untouched). Primary (held-out truedop_2024): 1.096 -> predicted 0.96-1.06, through usable_fix_rate for the first time since exp 5: 7.5% -> 10-15%, with false_fix_rate 17% -> 11-16% (members whose local descriptors encode the common picture agree on 2024 frames for the same reason they agree on training frames, so the confident set is enriched for correct fixes). 2024 coverage: 0.245 -> 0.27-0.38; the 0.2 FAIL floor is not expected to bind, because a shared canonical target should raise member agreement, not lower it. 2024 median error among confident frames (1,342 m) should fall below 800 m. train_capture_diagnostics (bb_dop20 / truedop_2022 / truedop_2023 = 0.833 / 0.845 / 0.703 on exp 7, usable 22 / 18 / 32%) are predicted to IMPROVE slightly to 0.60-0.80 (the auxiliary is also a regulariser for an underfit trunk, and the composite is 81-85% correlated with every training survey); the evidence that matters is the gap between those three numbers and the 2024 score narrowing, not the training numbers alone. Decision rules: (a) recon < 0.5 AND 2024 usable up by >= 3 points with false fix not rising -> supported; the next experiment either sharpens the target (64x64 at 2 m/px, or the composite's gradient-magnitude map so only edges count) or puts exp 5's whole-frame trunk on top, since its fit gain on the training surveys may now transfer. (b) recon < 0.5 but 2024 usable flat (<= 9%) -> the trunk carries the canonical structure for the decoder AND the survey cues for the head side by side in 112 dims; the next move is to make the head read the decoder's bottleneck (a capacity-allocation experiment), not another auxiliary. (c) recon stays >= 0.7 -> the decoder cannot paint 4 m/px structure from 31 px receptive-field features at weight 3, or the weight is too low; retry once with RECON_WEIGHT 10 before concluding anything (the term is bounded - MSE to a standardised target through a decoder - so, unlike exp 9's penalty, a 3x larger weight cannot produce a degenerate trunk). (d) 2024 coverage < 0.2 (FAIL) -> the auxiliary made the members disagree more on the foreign photograph; note it, and the next step is the same loss with the committee gate relaxed to the geometric mean of the two block masses, nothing else changed. Standing check: the score must move through usable_fix_rate; an improvement through false_fix_rate alone with usable flat means the composite taught honesty, not place - still kept, but rule (b) applies to the next design.
eli5: Three aerial photographs of the same Berlin street disagree about the parked cars, the shadows and the leaves on the trees, but they agree about the roads, the canals and the building footprints. We make a fourth picture of the whole city by majority vote, pixel by pixel: anything that appears in only one photograph simply vanishes, and what two or three agree on stays. During training, the two navigators are shown one real photograph of a place and asked to sketch, in coarse strokes, what that majority-vote picture of the place looks like. The only way to pass the sketching test is to notice the permanent features and ignore the fleeting ones, which is exactly the habit a navigator needs when the drone's own camera takes a fifth photograph nobody has. The sketching pad is thrown away before the model flies; only the habit stays.

stages.name: Camera frame
stages.detail: 128×128 px daytime crop, Berlin only; trained on three survey photographs, scored on a fourth it never saw

stages.name: Feature extractor
stages.detail: two independent small strided conv stacks (112 channels at the top), sharing no weights; each turns the frame into its own compact 112-number description of the place. Unchanged at inference; during training its 8×8 feature map, before pooling, is what the new sketching task reads

stages.name: Map-cell classifier
stages.detail: each extractor feeds its own scorer over all ~3,000 128 m map tiles of Berlin; the two tile-belief maps are averaged to pick the tile

stages.name: Local belief pooling
stages.detail: gathers the averaged belief spread over the winning tile AND its 8 neighbours, and places the fix at the balance point of that local cluster instead of snapping to one tile's centre

stages.name: Within-cell offset
stages.detail: small head per member that nudges the fix from the pooled balance point to the exact spot; the two nudges are averaged

stages.name: Confidence gate
stages.detail: confidence = the SMALLER of the two members' belief on the winning tile plus its 8 neighbours — both navigators must independently back the same place; if either one spreads its belief elsewhere the drone abstains

stages.name: Training signal
stages.detail: NEW: a fourth picture of Berlin is built once per run as the pixel-by-pixel majority vote (median) of the three training photographs, after matching their overall colour and brightness, so anything seen in only one photograph disappears. For every training view, each member's 8×8 feature map is fed to a small throw-away sketching head that must repaint that majority-vote picture of the same place at 4 m per pixel (brightness and colour balance removed from the target), and the member pays for the mismatch (weight 3) on top of its usual tile-and-offset loss. The sketching heads are discarded before export. Paired three-survey batches, re-photographing, targets, schedule and views per epoch unchanged.

implementation_brief:
GOAL: add a training-only reconstruction auxiliary to the two-member committee. The deployed graph (CellLocNet.forward, export_onnx) must be byte-identical to the current champion: exported berlin.onnx = 3,942,411 bytes. Nothing under model/ may open truedop_2024 or any capture with role 'eval' in any form; the composite is built ONLY from the tensors load_scene() already loads via buckets(meta, 'train').

=== model/model.py ===
1. Add constants next to CELL_PX / N_MEMBERS / MEMBER_CHANS:
   CANON_PX = 32          # composite target edge in px (128 px crop average-pooled 4x -> 4 m/px)
   RECON_WEIGHT = 3.0     # weight of the reconstruction MSE per member
2. class Member: keep forward(x) EXACTLY as it is (it is what CellLocNet.forward traces into the ONNX graph). Add:
   def forward_train(self, x):
       fmap = self.features(x)                 # [B, 112, 8, 8]
       f = fmap.mean(dim=(2, 3))
       return self.cls_head(f), torch.tanh(self.off_head(f)) * 0.5, fmap
   (Do not make forward() call forward_train(); leave forward() untouched so the traced graph cannot change.)
3. Add a training-only module (module-level class; NOT a submodule of CellLocNet, never referenced from CellLocNet or export_onnx):
   class CanonDecoder(nn.Module):
       """Training-only: repaints the canonical composite crop (CANON_PX square, 3 channels, standardised) from a member's 8x8 feature map. Discarded before export."""
       def __init__(self, cin=MEMBER_CHANS[-1]):
           super().__init__()
           self.net = nn.Sequential(
               nn.Conv2d(cin, 64, 3, padding=1), nn.BatchNorm2d(64), nn.ReLU(inplace=True),
               nn.Upsample(scale_factor=2, mode='nearest'),               # 8 -> 16
               nn.Conv2d(64, 32, 3, padding=1), nn.BatchNorm2d(32), nn.ReLU(inplace=True),
               nn.Upsample(scale_factor=2, mode='nearest'),               # 16 -> 32
               nn.Conv2d(32, 3, 3, padding=1))
       def forward(self, fmap):
           return self.net(fmap)                                          # [B, 3, 32, 32]
   def recon_loss_fn(pred, target):
       return F.mse_loss(pred, target)
4. Update the module docstring with a paragraph: 'CANONICAL-COMPOSITE RECONSTRUCTION (capture-holdout era, experiment 10, training-only)' describing the median composite target, the per-member CanonDecoder, that it never exports, and the probe numbers (survey<->survey 0.58-0.62 vs survey<->composite 0.81-0.85 at 4 m/px). Everything else in model.py (grid_dims, CellLocNet incl. block_mask/training_outputs/forward, build_model, loss_fn, export_onnx, estimate_position) stays untouched.

=== model/train.py ===
5. Imports: add CANON_PX, RECON_WEIGHT, CanonDecoder, recon_loss_fn to the `from model.model import (...)` line; `import torch.nn as nn` is needed for nn.ModuleList.
6. New function build_canonical(scene_u8: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor. Input: the resident training captures, uint8 [K,3,H,W] on the device (K = number of TRAIN captures, 3 for Berlin). Output: uint8 [1,3,H,W] on the same device. Steps, all on the device, processed in row slabs (e.g. 256 rows) so no float copy of a whole raster is ever resident (the M1 fallback must not OOM):
   a. per-survey per-channel mean and std over the whole raster: accumulate sum and sum-of-squares in float64 (or float32 with care) over slabs -> mean[K,3], std[K,3]; m_avg = mean.mean(0), s_avg = std.mean(0).
   b. per slab: norm = (slab.float() - mean[:, :, None, None]) / std[:, :, None, None] * s_avg[None, :, None, None] + m_avg[None, :, None, None]   # [K,3,h,W]
      med = norm.sort(dim=0).values[K // 2]   # per-pixel per-channel median across surveys; use sort, not torch.median, so it runs on MPS/CUDA/CPU alike (for K=3 index 1 is the exact median)
      out[:, :, rows] = med.clamp(0, 255).round().to(torch.uint8)
   c. print one line: '[area] canonical composite built from K training captures in X.Xs, channel means=[...]' (read means once, outside any step loop).
   Reference implementation of the same arithmetic in numpy: runs/_probe_exp10_canon.py (the 'composite' block). The eval capture is not in `scene` by construction (load_scene loads buckets(meta,'train') only) - keep it that way and say so in the docstring.
7. train_area(): after `scene = ...to(device)` and `del imgs`, add `canon = build_canonical(scene)`. Create the decoders AFTER build_model (so the members' random init under the seed is unchanged from exp 7): `decoders = nn.ModuleList(CanonDecoder() for _ in range(N_MEMBERS)).to(device)`. Optimiser: `opt = torch.optim.Adam(list(model.parameters()) + list(decoders.parameters()), lr=1e-3)`; scheduler unchanged (CosineAnnealingLR, T_max=epochs, eta_min=1e-4). Pass `canon` and `decoders` into run_epoch.
8. run_epoch(): add parameters `canon, decoders`; call `decoders.train()` next to `model.train()`. Add a device accumulator `recon_sum = torch.zeros(N_MEMBERS, device=device)`. Inside the mini-batch loop, right after xb0 is cut:
   tgt = gpu_crops(canon, torch.zeros_like(cap_b), cx[idx], cy[idx], ang[idx])   # [B,3,128,128] in [0,1], same geometry as the inputs
   tgt = F.avg_pool2d(tgt, CROP_PX // CANON_PX)                                   # [B,3,32,32], 4 m/px
   tgt = (tgt - tgt.mean(dim=(2, 3), keepdim=True)) / (tgt.std(dim=(2, 3), keepdim=True) + 0.02)   # per crop per channel; eps 0.02 (~5/255) keeps flat water/roof crops from amplifying noise
   Computed ONCE per mini-batch (shared by both members: clean composite, no augmentation, same geometry). Then in the member loop replace `logits_k, off_k = member(xb_k)` with `logits_k, off_k, fmap_k = member.forward_train(xb_k)` and add:
   rec_k = recon_loss_fn(decoders[k](fmap_k), tgt)
   loss = loss + loss_fn(logits_k, off_k, soft_t, off_t_k) + RECON_WEIGHT * rec_k
   and under torch.no_grad(): recon_sum[k] += rec_k.detach() * B   (iterate members with enumerate to get k). Keep every existing stat (member_correct, agree, cap_correct, conf_sum) exactly as is. No .item()/.cpu()/float() inside the step loop. Return 'recon_sum': recon_sum.cpu().tolist() in the stats dict.
9. Logging: per-epoch print line gains ` recon=[a, b]` = recon_sum[k]/seen rounded to 4 (chance level is 1.0 by construction; the pre-registered check is < 0.5 at epoch 8 for both). train_info additions: 'recon_weight': RECON_WEIGHT, 'canon_px': CANON_PX, 'final_recon': [per member], 'canonical_target': 'per-pixel per-channel median of the globally colour-normalised TRAINING captures, cut at the view geometry, avg-pooled to 32x32, standardised per crop per channel; decoder training-only, never exported', and extend the 'capture_sampling' string with ', canonical-composite reconstruction auxiliary per member'. Update the module docstring with a CANONICAL-COMPOSITE RECONSTRUCTION paragraph.
10. Export unchanged: `export_onnx(model.cpu(), str(onnx_path))` - the decoders are simply never exported. Assert nothing else; the harness checks bytes.

=== Contracts to preserve (frozen scorer depends on them) ===
- CLI: `python -m model.train --area <a> --out-dir <d> [--data-dir D] [--epochs N] [--max-crops-per-bucket M] [--seed S]`; writes <out>/models/<area>.onnx and appends to <out>/train_info.json; prints the info JSON last.
- ONNX: input 'frame' 1x3x128x128 float32 in [0,1] -> output 'uvc' [[u, v, conf]], u/v normalised map coords, conf in [0,1]; opset 17, dynamo=False; whole decode inside the graph; exported file must be 3,942,411 bytes and pass the 4 MiB / 250 ms gates.
- Training reads only buckets(meta, 'train'); truedop_2024 is never opened by anything under model/.
- Files in /FROZEN (pipeline/, scorer, dataset) are not touched.
- Cost: one extra gpu_crops call and two tiny decoder passes per step; expect <= 15% over exp 7's 399 s per 8-epoch run on the L4. Keep BATCH_SIZE, CHUNK_SIZE, AUG, schedule, epochs as they are.
